description: Teach-mode + passive coaching during history. Educational only.

modules.title: Constipation history structure
points: Establish baseline bowel habit, stool consistency (Bristol scale), and whether this represents a genuine change from normal.
New constipation in an older adult, especially with weight loss or rectal bleeding, is an alarm pattern until colorectal cancer is excluded.
Screen medication causes (opioids, anticholinergics, iron, calcium channel blockers) before assuming a primary functional cause.

modules.title: Constipation alarm features
points: New change in bowel habit with rectal bleeding, weight loss, or a palpable mass warrants colonoscopy rather than empirical laxative therapy alone.

Q000091.why_ask: A genuine, sustained change in bowel habit is far more concerning than lifelong mild constipation.
Q000091.think: New change in an older adult should not be attributed to diet/lifestyle without further evaluation.

Q000035.why_ask: Rectal bleeding alongside constipation should never be attributed to haemorrhoids without examination.
listen_for: on the stool vs mixed in
Q000035.think: Combine with age and family history to decide on colonoscopy referral.

answer_triggers.title: Unlocked: new change in bowel habit
points: This is an alarm feature, particularly in patients over 50.
Ensure rectal bleeding and weight loss have been specifically asked about.
